request: how does a hash table work?

composition.story: How does a hash table retrieve a value without scanning every entry? Start with three stored entries and request “act.” Hash the key, follow its bucket, and compare the chained keys. Watch “cat” fail before “act” matches: sharing a bucket never makes two keys interchangeable.

aha.observation: Hashing selects a bucket; exact key comparison distinguishes colliding keys and retrieves the correct value.

Highlight only the bound active regions. Bucket labels are zero-based addresses. Fixed inputs use case-sensitive keys and an intentionally weak character-count hash. Separate chaining preserves entry order. No insertion, deletion, or resizing occurs. Reserve label space at native width; do not animate.
Anchor text beside its target without covering entries. Callout text identifies location only. Put the bound reason above the experiment.

Place compact readouts below the picture. Render Status as the bound status line. Hash outputs are zero-based bucket indices. Comparisons count exact key-equality tests; integers require no rounding. Balanced parameter-control budget: zero, excluding navigation and reset.

states.label: Request the key
states.why: The table already stores its entries. Use Next to look up act without scanning the entire table.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Ready to hash the requested key.

states.label: Compute the bucket
states.why: The requested key has three characters. Its character count modulo the bucket count determines the bucket address.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Bucket address computed; no stored keys compared.

states.label: Follow the bucket
states.why: Only this bucket's chain needs searching. The pear entry belongs to another bucket and remains untouched.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Follow the selected bucket's head link.

states.label: Reject the colliding key
states.why: Cat and act share a hash output, but their keys differ. Follow Next within the chain instead of returning feline.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Key mismatch; continue along the same chain.

states.label: Return the matching value
states.why: The exact key matches. Hashing narrowed the search; key comparison distinguished the colliding entries and selected the correct value.

readouts.label: Status
readouts.value: Lookup complete; pear was never compared.
